title: SDK sandbox jotter — quick fixes & tiny experiments
content:
Context: personal scratchpad for small, actionable SDK/docs fixes I can do in short chunks. Mostly for onboarding tasks, tiny sample apps, and a couple of tutorial flows that keep breaking during user testing. Keeping this intentionally informal — quick notes, time-boxed todos, and experiment results.

Goals for this sprint (today):
- Triage 3 micro-bugs in the JS quickstart that confuse users (10–30m each).
- Add a second sample app that demonstrates streaming + function-calling (45–90m).
- Capture 5 doc gaps to hand off to docs eng for next week.

Notes / discoveries (raw):
- Quickstart mismatch: README shows `client.generate()` example but the current SDK is `client.text.generate()` (API surface changed in v0.9.1). Users hit a TypeError.
  - Temporary fix: update README snippet to correct call and add a one-line note: "See API surface changes in changelog v0.9.1".
  - Ticket: JIRA-INF-472 (linked).

- Windows curl example in embeddings tutorial uses single quotes which breaks on cmd.exe. Need to provide both POSIX and Windows variants.
  - Add small table: curl (bash) vs curl (powershell).

- The streaming sample (chat-stream.md) omits how to handle reconnects when using a proxy. Users report truncated replies when corporate proxy drops connection mid-stream.
  - Short-term: add "reconnect pattern" pseudo-code block.
  - Longer-term: sample app that demonstrates resume with partial KV-cache + idempotent request ids.

Micro-todo list (ordered by impact & time estimate):
[ ] Update JS quickstart README (5–10m) — fix client call, add tiny note about versions. PR: draft branch `ivy/quickstart-fix`
[ ] Add Windows curl examples to embeddings tutorial (10–20m) — create snippet and push to `docs/embeddings/windows-curl`
[ ] Write reconnect snippet for streaming page (20–30m) — include Node and Python examples
[ ] Create minimal streaming+function-calling sample app (45–90m) — goal: runnable with Docker, shows server-side function registration and streaming responses to client
[ ] Run through sample app on mac + linux CI (30–60m) — CI matrix flake check
[ ] Capture doc gaps list and create JIRA tickets (15–20m)

Sample app outline (stream-fn-demo):
- Purpose: show streaming tokens while also invoking external tools via function calling and streaming partial function outputs back to client.
- Files: server.js (Node express + sdk client), functions/weather.js (dummy function), client.html (simple SSE or fetch streaming display).
- Local run: Dockerfile + `docker-compose up` that spins up server and serves client on 3000.
- Key bits to highlight in README: how to set SDK_KEY, how to enable streaming, how to register functions, basic latency expectations.

Small code snippets for the reconnect pattern (place in docs):
- Node (pseudo):
  const res = fetch(streamUrl, { headers });
  try { for await (const chunk of res.body) { processChunk(chunk) } } catch (e) { // on network error, retry with backoff, use last event id to resume }

- Python (pseudo):
  resp = requests.get(stream_url, stream=True)
  try:
    for chunk in resp.iter_lines():
      if chunk: handle(chunk)
  except requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError:
    # retry logic here

Doc gaps (short list to hand to docs team):
1) API surface diff note: quickstart examples across languages don't reflect v0.9.x rename of top-level generation methods. Provide a compatibility note.
2) Windows CLI examples: add PowerShell/cmd variants for all curl snippets.
3) Streaming reconnect patterns: one page with idiomatic retry behavior + how caching interacts with resume.
4) Function-calling example: more complete sample showing function schema + error handling (timeouts, partial results).
5) Env & config: clear checklist for Docker/local development (ports, env vars, minimum SDK version).

User feedback snippets (copied from Slack):
- @marco: "Quickstart example blew up for me — had to dig into CHANGELOG to find client.rename — painful."
- @leah: "Streaming stopped halfway, client had no idea how to reconnect — docs are quiet on that."

Blocking questions for the week (need from infra/docs):
- Do we want the sample apps to rely on hosted API keys for quickstart, or include mock server so users can run offline? Pros/cons: hosted = fastest demo, but flaky for offline workshops. Mock server = more code but reliable demo. Preference: include mock server as optional mode.
- Who will own the Windows curl PR? (ask docs eng).

Small experiments I want to run (time-boxed):
- A/B two READMEs for quickstart: one that defaults to hosted-key flow vs one that uses a local mock server. Measure user-reported friction from internal playtests (15–30m to set up).
- Try embedding short-run-time code coverage that highlights which README sections new users read (instrumentation via short link clicks).

Next actions (today):
1) Push README fix branch `ivy/quickstart-fix` and open PR -> assign Marco for review.
2) Draft Windows curl snippets and paste in this doc for quick copy -> then open small docs PR.
3) Prototype streaming+function demo repo skeleton (create README + server stub).

Random notes / reminders to self:
- Keep examples under 50 lines where possible — lower cognitive load in docs.
- Add a "when things go wrong" short troubleshooting section to streaming docs (common errors + quick fixes).
- Follow up with Leah about CI failures that happened yesterday on linux runner (she mentioned flaky Docker startup).

Timeboxing: if any task hits 45m and not finished, stop and move to next highest impact. These are micro-wins to improve onboarding quickly.

End of jotter — will convert to a proper PR checklist once I have a green CI run and the sample app prototype.
